children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to know about your child's age, as this determines the eligibility path.

**Could you please tell me:**
1. Do you have a child (or children) you're applying for?
2. How old is your child?

The age categories are:
- **Under 16** - generally eligible (with some conditions)
- **16-19** - may be eligible if in approved education or training
- **20 or over** - not eligible for Child Benefit

Please share your child's age and I'll guide you through the rest of the eligibility check.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to apply for Child Benefit for my child Alex, who is 3 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Let me check the eligibility for Alex, who is 3 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, they fall into the category that generally qualifies for Child Benefit. However, I need to check a few more conditions.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to confirm:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Since Alex is only 3 years old, I assume they're not in paid work, but I need to confirm this to proceed with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex isn't working at all - he's only 3!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes sense. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

This refers to benefits like Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit that would be claimed in the child's own name (which is very rare for young children). 

For a 3-year-old like Alex, this would be extremely uncommon. Can you confirm that Alex is not receiving any such benefits in his own name?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent, let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is only 3 years old, he wouldn't be in an apprenticeship program. I just need to confirm this to proceed.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any apprenticeship - he's far too young for that!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely right! Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status, as this is a key requirement for Child Benefit.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You can qualify if ANY of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK**
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself and family
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Which of these applies to your situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That satisfies the residency requirement. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You qualify if ANY of the following applies:

1. **You live with Alex**
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep (paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be, or equivalent in kind - such as food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents)
3. You pay maintenance for Alex under a court order or agreement that equals or exceeds Child Benefit payments

**Which of these applies to your situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another relative or guardian
- Anyone else who cares for Alex

Please note:
- Only ONE person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time
- If someone else is claiming but you both agree that you should claim instead, that's fine - they would just need to stop their claim
- If there's a dispute about who should claim, HMRC would need to decide

**What is your situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Which of the following describes Alex's current situation?**

1. **Living normally at home with you** (standard situation)
2. In hospital
3. In local authority care
4. Being fostered

Since you mentioned Alex lives with you at home in Manchester, I'm assuming this is a normal living arrangement - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex lives at home with me in a normal living arrangement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
One final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you covering Alex's living costs yourself (without the local council paying for his accommodation or maintenance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I'm covering all of Alex's costs myself. The council isn't paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me get the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Result: ELIGIBLE** ✓

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for Alex.

### Why You're Eligible:

You've satisfied all the necessary criteria:
- ✓ Alex is 3 years old (under 16)
- ✓ Alex is not in paid work
- ✓ Alex is not receiving benefits in his own right
- ✓ Alex is not in an apprenticeship
- ✓ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✓ You're responsible for Alex (living with him)
- ✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✓ Alex lives at home in a normal arrangement
- ✓ The local council isn't paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or your partner earns over £60,000, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through the tax system
5. **Payments** will be made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### More Information:
You can apply and find more details at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the application process?
